entries.title: Jeremiah 41:1
segments:
. ISHMAEL MURDERS GEDALIAH AND OTHERS, THEN FLEES TO THE AMMONITES. JOHANAN PURSUES HIM, RECOVERS THE CAPTIVES, AND PURPOSES TO FLEE TO EGYPT FOR FEAR OF THE CHALDEANS. 
 
    1. seventh month--the second month after the burning of the city (

). 
 
    and the princes--not the nominative. And the princes came, for the "princes" are not mentioned either in
or in

: but, "Ishmael being of the seed royal and of the princes of the king" [MAURER]. But the ten men were the "princes of the king"; thus MAURER'S objection has no weight: so English Version. 
 
    eat bread together--Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, by whom he was hospitably received, in violation of the sacred right of hospitality (

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:2
segments: 2. slew him whom the king of Babylon had made governor--This assigns a reason for their slaying him, as well as showing the magnitude of their crime (

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:3
segments: 3. slew all the Jews--namely, the attendants and ministers of Gedaliah; or, the military alone, about his person; translate, "even (not 'and,' as English Version) the men of war." The main portion of the people with Gedaliah, including Jeremiah, Ishmael carried away captive (

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:4
segments: 4. no man knew it--that is, outside Mizpah. Before tidings of the murder had gone abroad.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:5
segments:
5. beards shaven, &c.--indicating their deep sorrow at the destruction of the temple and city. 
 
    cut themselves--a heathen custom, forbidden (

). The place in which a temple had stood, even when it had been destroyed, was held sacred [PAPINIAN]. Those "from Shiloh" would naturally seek the house of the Lord, since it was at Shiloh it originally was set up (

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:6
segments:
6. weeping--pretending to weep, as they did, for the ruin of the temple. 
 
    Come to Gedaliah--as if he was one of Gedaliah's retinue.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:7
segments: 7. and cast them into ... pit--He had not killed them in the pit (compare
); these words are therefore rightly supplied in English Version. "The pit" or cistern made by Asa to guard against a want of water when Baasha was about to besiege the city (
). The trench or fosse round the city [GROTIUS]. Ishmael's motive for the murder seems to have been a suspicion that they were coming to live under Gedaliah.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:8
segments:
8. treasures--It was customary to hide grain in cavities underground in troubled times. "We have treasures," which we will give, if our lives be spared. 
 
    slew ... not-- (
). Ishmael's avarice and needs overcame his cruelty.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:9
segments: 9. because of Gedaliah--rather, "near Gedaliah," namely, those intercepted by Ishmael on their way from Samaria to Jerusalem and killed at Mizpah, where Gedaliah had lived. So
, "next";

, Margin, literally, as here, "at his hand." "In the reign of Gedaliah" [CALVIN]. However, English Version gives a good sense: Ishmael's reason for killing them was because of his supposing them to be connected with Gedaliah.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:10
segments: 10. the king's daughters-- (
). Zedekiah's. Ishmael must have got additional followers (whom the hope of gain attracted), besides those who originally set out with him (
), so as to have been able to carry off all the residue of the people. He probably meant to sell them as slaves to the Ammonites (see on

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:11
segments: 11. Johanan--the friend of Gedaliah who had warned him of Ishmael's treachery, but in vain (

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:12
segments: 12. the ... waters-- (

); a large reservoir or lake. 
 
    in Gibeon--on the road from Mizpah to Ammon: one of the sacerdotal cities of Benjamin, four miles northwest of Jerusalem, now Eljib.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:13
segments: 13. glad--at the prospect of having a deliverer from their captivity.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:14
segments: 14. cast about--came round.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:16
segments: 16. men of war--"The men of war," stated in

to have been slain by Ishmael, must refer to the military about Gedaliah's person; "the men of war" here to those not so. 
 
    eunuchs--The kings of Judah had adopted the bad practice of having harems and eunuchs from the surrounding heathen kingdoms.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:17
segments: 17. dwelt--for a time, until they were ready for their journey to Egypt (

). 
 
    habitation to Chimham--his "caravanserai" close by Beth-lehem. David, in reward for Barzillai's loyalty, took Chimham his son under his patronage, and made over to him his own patrimony in the land of Beth-lehem. It was thence called the habitation of Chimham (Geruth-Chimham), though it reverted to David's heirs in the year of jubilee. "Caravanserais" (a compound Persian word, meaning "the house of a company of travellers") differ from our inns, in that there is no host to supply food, but each traveller must carry with him his own.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:18
segments: 18. afraid--lest the Chaldeans should suspect all the Jews of being implicated in Ishmael's treason, as though the Jews sought to have a prince of the house of David (

). Their better way towards gaining God's favor would have been to have laid the blame on the real culprit, and to have cleared themselves. A tortuous policy is the parent of fear. Righteousness inspires with boldness (
